# dybatpho function reference

> Every public `dybatpho::` function, grouped by module, with its signature
> and the first sentence of its description. A signature lists argument types
> in order: `<type>` is required, `[type]` optional, `type...` repeats,
> and `[options]` takes flags first. The full reference of a module is
> docs/<module>.md.

Generated by `scripts/docs.sh` from the source comments; see
[llms.txt](llms.txt) for how to load the library.

## init

Initial script. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/init.md](docs/init.md)

- `dybatpho::export_functions` — Make the loaded library available to child Bash processes.
- `dybatpho::version` — Print the version of the library this shell loaded, including the commit it is at.
- `dybatpho::load <string...>` — Load one or more modules after `init.sh` has already been sourced.
- `dybatpho::module_loaded <string>` — Return success when a module is already loaded.
- `dybatpho::module_list [string]` — Print module names, one per line.
- `dybatpho::module_tier <string>` — Print the stability tier of a module.

## agent

Utilities for making a script usable by an AI agent. Loaded: `--modules agent`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/agent.md](docs/agent.md)

- `dybatpho::agent_mode` — Print whether this run is being driven by an agent.
- `dybatpho::agent_detect` — Return success when an agent is driving this run.
- `dybatpho::agent_result <string> <string...>` — Report the outcome of an operation in the caller's language.
- `dybatpho::agent_error <string> <string> [string]` — Report a failure with a machine-readable code and a fix hint.
- `dybatpho::agent_context` — Describe the environment an agent is operating in.
- `dybatpho::agent_confirm <string> [string]` — Gate an action behind confirmation, or behind an allowlist.
- `dybatpho::agent_audit <string> [string]` — Append one action to the audit log.
- `dybatpho::agent_audit_show` — Print the audit log as readable lines.
- `dybatpho::agent_tools <string> [string] [string]` — Generate tool definitions from a CLI option spec.
- `dybatpho::agent_mcp <string> [string] [string]` — Generate an MCP `tools/list` payload for a CLI option spec.
- `dybatpho::agent_mcp_serve <string> [string] [string]` — Serve a script's commands as MCP tools over stdio.

## ai

Utilities for calling large language models from shell scripts. Loaded: `--modules ai`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/ai.md](docs/ai.md)

- `dybatpho::ai_provider` — Resolve which backend a call will use.
- `dybatpho::ai_model [string]` — Resolve the model identifier for the active backend.
- `dybatpho::ai_check` — Report whether the module can run, without making a request.
- `dybatpho::ai_cache_clear` — Forget every cached response.
- `dybatpho::ai_ask <string> [string]` — Ask the model a single question and print its answer.
- `dybatpho::ai_conversation_new <string> [string]` — Create a conversation file and store its path in a variable.
- `dybatpho::ai_conversation_add <string> <string> <string>` — Append a turn to a conversation file.
- `dybatpho::ai_conversation_show <string>` — Print a conversation as readable transcript lines.
- `dybatpho::ai_chat <string> <string>` — Send the next turn of a stored conversation and record the reply.
- `dybatpho::ai_json <string> <string> [string]` — Ask for an answer that matches a JSON schema, and validate it.
- `dybatpho::ai_stream <string> [string]` — Ask a question and print the answer as it is generated.
- `dybatpho::ai_tool_register <string> <string> <string> <string>` — Register a shell function the model may call during `ai_run`.
- `dybatpho::ai_tool_list` — Print the names of registered tools, one per line.
- `dybatpho::ai_tool_clear` — Unregister every tool.
- `dybatpho::ai_run <string> [string]` — Answer a prompt, letting the model call registered tools first.
- `dybatpho::ai_tokens_estimate <string>` — Estimate how many tokens a piece of text costs.
- `dybatpho::ai_usage [string]` — Print the token usage recorded so far.
- `dybatpho::ai_usage_field <string>` — Read one usage counter as a bare value.
- `dybatpho::ai_usage_reset` — Reset every usage counter and the call budget consumption.
- `dybatpho::ai_budget <number>` — Cap how many model calls the rest of the script may make.
- `dybatpho::ai_redact <string>` — Redact secrets and common personal identifiers in text.
- `dybatpho::ai_untrusted <string> [string]` — Wrap text that came from outside the script -- a log, a diff, a web page, a tool's output -- so the model can tell it apart from the script's own instructions.

## archive

Utilities for creating, extracting, and listing archives. Loaded: `--modules archive`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/archive.md](docs/archive.md)

- `dybatpho::archive_create <string> <string>` — Create an archive from a file or directory.
- `dybatpho::archive_extract <string> [string] [number]` — Extract an archive into a target directory.
- `dybatpho::archive_list <string>` — List the contents of an archive without extracting it.
- `dybatpho::archive_unsafe_entries <string>` — List archive entries that would escape the extraction directory: a path that is absolute or climbs out through `..`, and a symbolic link whose target is absolute or has a `..` component.
- `dybatpho::archive_is_safe <string>` — Return success when no archive entry escapes the extraction directory.

## array

Utilities for working with array. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/array.md](docs/array.md)

- `dybatpho::array_print <string>` — Print each element of an array on its own line.
- `dybatpho::array_reverse <string> <string>` — Reverse an array in place.
- `dybatpho::array_unique <string> <string>` — Remove duplicate elements from an array in place, keeping the first occurrence of each value.
- `dybatpho::array_contains <string> <string>` — Return success when an array contains the given element.
- `dybatpho::array_index_of <string> <string>` — Print the first index of an array element that matches exactly.
- `dybatpho::array_compact <string> <string>` — Remove empty-string elements from an array in place.
- `dybatpho::array_filter <string> <string> <string>` — Keep only array elements accepted by a predicate function.
- `dybatpho::array_map <string> <string> <string>` — Transform each array element with a mapper function.
- `dybatpho::array_find <string> <string>` — Print the first array element accepted by a predicate function.
- `dybatpho::array_every <string> <string>` — Return success when every array element is accepted by a predicate function.
- `dybatpho::array_some <string> <string>` — Return success when at least one array element is accepted by a predicate function.
- `dybatpho::array_reject <string> <string> <string>` — Keep only array elements rejected by a predicate function.
- `dybatpho::array_first <string>` — Print the first element of an array.
- `dybatpho::array_last <string>` — Print the last element of an array.
- `dybatpho::array_join <string> <string>` — Join array elements with a separator into one string.
- `dybatpho::array_sort <string> <string...>` — Sort an array in place.
- `dybatpho::array_slice <string> <number> [number] <string>` — Keep a run of an array in place and drop the rest.
- `dybatpho::array_union <string> <string> <string>` — Replace an array with the union of it and another, in place.
- `dybatpho::array_intersect <string> <string> <string>` — Keep only the values an array shares with another, in place.
- `dybatpho::array_difference <string> <string> <string>` — Drop the values an array shares with another, in place.
- `dybatpho::array_toposort <string> <string> [string...]` — Order a dependency graph so every entry comes after the entries it depends on.
- `dybatpho::array_closure <string> <string> <string...>` — Collect everything reachable from some roots in a dependency graph, the roots included.

## backup

Utilities for taking backups and applying a retention policy. Loaded: `--modules backup`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/backup.md](docs/backup.md)

- `dybatpho::backup_create <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Take a timestamped backup of a file or directory.
- `dybatpho::backup_list <string> [string]` — List a directory's backups, newest first.
- `dybatpho::backup_latest <string> [string]` — Print the most recent backup in a directory.
- `dybatpho::backup_verify <string>` — Check a backup against its checksum sidecar.
- `dybatpho::backup_restore <string> <string> <string>` — Restore a backup into a target directory.
- `dybatpho::backup_prune [options] <string> <string...>` — Delete the backups a retention policy does not keep.
- `dybatpho::backup_diff [options] <string> <string>` — Show what changed between two backups, or between a backup and the live data it was taken from.

## cache

Utilities for remembering an answer on disk until it goes stale. Loaded: `--modules cache`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/cache.md](docs/cache.md)

- `dybatpho::cache_dir` — Print the directory entries are written to.
- `dybatpho::cache_key <string...>` — Turn any values into a key that is safe as a file name.
- `dybatpho::cache_path <string>` — Print the path an entry is stored at.
- `dybatpho::cache_has <string> [number]` — Return success when an entry exists and is still fresh.
- `dybatpho::cache_get <string> [number]` — Print an entry when it is still fresh.
- `dybatpho::cache_set <string>` — Store standard input as an entry.
- `dybatpho::cache_forget <string>` — Remove one entry.
- `dybatpho::cache_clear` — Remove every entry in the current namespace.
- `dybatpho::cache_wait <string> [number]` — Wait until no background refresh of an entry is running.
- `dybatpho::cache_run <string> [number] [string...]` — Print what a command prints, running it only when the remembered answer has gone stale.
- `dybatpho::cache_prune <string...>` — Remove old entries until the namespace fits the limits given.
- `dybatpho::cache_stats [number] [string...]` — Describe the current namespace: how many entries it holds, how many bytes they take, how many are still fresh, and how old the oldest and newest are.

## cli

Utilities for building CLI parsers from shell specs.. Loaded: `--modules cli`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md)

- `dybatpho::prompt <string> [string]` — Read a line from the terminal (or stdin) with an optional default.
- `dybatpho::select <string> <string> <bool>` — Prompt for one or more values from a comma-separated list or numeric range.
- `dybatpho::opts::validate_choice <string> <string>` — Check that a value belongs to a comma-separated choice list.
- `dybatpho::cli_levenshtein <string> <string>` — Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings.
- `dybatpho::cli_suggest <string> <string...>` — Print the candidates closest to a mistyped switch or command name.
- `dybatpho::cli_verbosity_level [number] [string]` — Raise a log level by the number of times a counting `-v` flag was repeated.
- `dybatpho::cli_apply_verbosity [number] [string]` — Apply a repeat count from a counting `-v` flag to `DYBATPHO_LOG_LEVEL`.
- `dybatpho::generate_schema <string> [string]` — Generate a JSON CLI schema from the same option spec used by parsing.
- `dybatpho::generate_man <string> [string]` — Generate a roff man page from a CLI option spec.
- `dybatpho::generate_completion <string> <string> [string]` — Generate Bash, Zsh, or Fish completion from a CLI option spec.
- `dybatpho::opts::setup <string> <string> <key:value...>` — Setup global settings for getting options (mandatory) in spec of script or function
- `dybatpho::opts::flag <string> <string> <switch|key:value...>` — Define an option that take no argument
- `dybatpho::opts::param <string> <string> <switch|key:value...>` — Define an option that take an argument
- `dybatpho::opts::disp <string> <switch|key:value...>` — Define an option that display only
- `dybatpho::opts::msg <string...>` — Place a line of free text in the generated help, so a long option list can be broken into labelled groups.
- `dybatpho::opts::cmd <string> <string> [key:value...]` — Define a sub-command in spec
- `dybatpho::opts::arg <string> <string> [key:value...]` — Declare a positional argument.
- `dybatpho::generate_from_spec <string>` — Define spec of parent function or script, spec contains below commands
- `dybatpho::generate_help <string>` — Show help description of root command/sub-command.

## config

Utilities for loading configuration from files and environment variables.. Loaded: `--modules config`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/config.md](docs/config.md)

- `dybatpho::config_load [string] <string...>` — Load one or more configuration files, merging them left to right.
- `dybatpho::config_profile <string> [string]` — Load a base configuration file and the profile overlay beside it.
- `dybatpho::config_env [string]` — Load environment variables after an optional prefix.
- `dybatpho::config_set <string> <string>` — Set a configuration value in memory.
- `dybatpho::config_get <string> [string]` — Print a configuration value.
- `dybatpho::config_ini_get <string> <string> [string]` — Print one value from an INI file, without loading the file into the configuration.
- `dybatpho::config_require <string...>` — Require configuration keys to be present.
- `dybatpho::config_export [string]` — Export loaded values as shell variables.
- `dybatpho::config_save <string> <string...>` — Write configuration values back to a file, in the format that file already uses.
- `dybatpho::config_schema <string> <string> <string...>` — Declare validation rules for a configuration key.
- `dybatpho::config_schema_reset` — Forget every declared configuration schema.
- `dybatpho::config_validate` — Validate configured values against all declared schemas.
- `dybatpho::config_doc [string] [string]` — Render documentation for every declared configuration key.

## csv

Utilities for reading, filtering and writing CSV data. Loaded: `--modules csv`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/csv.md](docs/csv.md)

- `dybatpho::csv_read <string> <string>` — Parse CSV into an array of records.
- `dybatpho::csv_fields <string> <string>` — Split one record from `dybatpho::csv_read` into a named array of field values.
- `dybatpho::csv_write <string>` — Serialize records back to CSV.
- `dybatpho::csv_convert <string> <string>` — Rewrite CSV with another delimiter.
- `dybatpho::csv_header <string>` — Print the column names from the first record.
- `dybatpho::csv_col <string> <string>` — Print one column's values, chosen by its header name or by its 1-based position when no header carries that name.
- `dybatpho::csv_select <string> <string...>` — Print chosen columns, in the order given, as CSV with the header.
- `dybatpho::csv_sort <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Sort the data rows by one column and print them as CSV with the header first.
- `dybatpho::csv_join <string> <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Join two CSV inputs on a key column and print the result as CSV.
- `dybatpho::csv_filter <string> <string> <string> <string>` — Keep the rows whose column satisfies a comparison, and print them as CSV with the header.
- `dybatpho::csv_to_json <string>` — Convert CSV to a JSON array of objects, keyed by the header.
- `dybatpho::csv_from_json <string>` — Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV.

## date

Utilities for working with dates and timestamps. Loaded: `--modules date`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/date.md](docs/date.md)

- `dybatpho::date_now [string]` — Print the current time using a `date` format string.
- `dybatpho::date_today [string]` — Print today's date using a `date` format string.
- `dybatpho::date_is_valid <string>` — Return success when a date string can be parsed by `date`.
- `dybatpho::date_parse <string>` — Parse a date string and print its Unix timestamp.
- `dybatpho::date_format <number> [string]` — Format a Unix timestamp with a `date` format string.
- `dybatpho::date_add_days <string> <number> [string]` — Add or subtract days from a date string and print the result.
- `dybatpho::date_diff_days <string> <string>` — Print the whole-day difference between two date strings.
- `dybatpho::date_is_leap_year <number>` — Return success when a year is a leap year.
- `dybatpho::date_days_in_month <number> <number>` — Print how many days a month has.
- `dybatpho::date_month_start <string> [string]` — Print the first day of the month a date falls in.
- `dybatpho::date_month_end <string> [string]` — Print the last day of the month a date falls in.
- `dybatpho::date_add <string> <number> <string> [string]` — Add or subtract a span of time from a date string.
- `dybatpho::date_diff <string> <string> [string]` — Print the difference between two dates in a chosen unit.
- `dybatpho::date_seconds_to_hms <number>` — Print a number of seconds as `H:MM:SS`.
- `dybatpho::date_parse_duration <string> <string>` — Parse a written length of time into a number of seconds.
- `dybatpho::date_is_before <string> <string>` — Return success when the first date comes strictly before the second.
- `dybatpho::date_is_after <string> <string>` — Return success when the first date comes strictly after the second.
- `dybatpho::date_iso_week <string> [string]` — Print the ISO 8601 week a date falls in.
- `dybatpho::date_in_tz <string> <string> [string]` — Print a date as it reads in another timezone.

## db

Utilities for keeping a script's state in SQLite. Loaded: `--modules db`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/db.md](docs/db.md)

- `dybatpho::db_exec <path> <string> <string...>` — Run SQL that changes the database, with bound parameters, in one transaction: either every statement takes effect or none does.
- `dybatpho::db_query <path> <string> <string...>` — Run SQL and print its rows as one JSON array of objects, `[]` for none.
- `dybatpho::db_value <path> <string> <string...>` — Run SQL and print the one value it yields, as it is.
- `dybatpho::db_migrate <path> <path>` — Apply the migrations of a directory not applied yet: the files named `<number>_<name>.sql`, in numeric order, each in its own transaction that records it in `dybatpho_migrations` first.

## diff

Utilities for comparing text and structured documents. Loaded: `--modules diff`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/diff.md](docs/diff.md)

- `dybatpho::diff_text <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Compare two texts and print a colored unified diff.
- `dybatpho::diff_summary <string> <string>` — Summarize a text comparison as one line.
- `dybatpho::diff_json <string> <string>` — Compare two JSON documents by key rather than by line.
- `dybatpho::diff_yaml <string> <string>` — Compare two YAML documents by key rather than by line.
- `dybatpho::diff_dir [options] <string> <string>` — Compare two directory trees entry by entry.

## doctor

Utilities for checking that the environment can run what a script loaded. Loaded: `--modules doctor`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/doctor.md](docs/doctor.md)

- `dybatpho::doctor_requirements <string> [string]` — Print the external commands a module can call.
- `dybatpho::doctor_bash_supported` — Return success when the running Bash is new enough for the library.
- `dybatpho::doctor <string...>` — Report the environment the loaded modules need, and what is missing.

## file

Utilities for file handling. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/file.md](docs/file.md)

- `dybatpho::show_file <string>` — Show the contents of a file with line numbers.
- `dybatpho::path_dirname <string>` — Return the directory component of a path.
- `dybatpho::path_basename <string> [string]` — Return the basename component of a path.
- `dybatpho::path_extname <string>` — Return the final extension of a path, including the leading dot.
- `dybatpho::path_stem <string>` — Return the basename of a path without its final extension.
- `dybatpho::path_join <string...>` — Join path segments with single `/` separators.
- `dybatpho::path_normalize <string>` — Normalize a path by collapsing repeated separators and resolving `.` and `..` textually.
- `dybatpho::path_is_abs <string>` — Return success when a path is absolute.
- `dybatpho::path_has_ext <string> [string]` — Return success when a path has any extension or a matching exact extension.
- `dybatpho::path_change_ext <string> <string>` — Return a path with its final extension replaced.
- `dybatpho::path_relative <string> <string>` — Return the relative path from a base path to a target path.
- `dybatpho::create_temp <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Create a temporary file or directory and register it for cleanup on shell exit.
- `dybatpho::file_write_atomic <string>` — Write standard input to a file through a staging file, so that readers see either the previous contents or the complete new contents.
- `dybatpho::file_replace <string> <string> <string>` — Substitute every match of a pattern in a file, in place.
- `dybatpho::file_ensure_line <string> <string>` — Append a line to a file unless the exact line is already there.
- `dybatpho::file_remove_line <string> <string>` — Remove every occurrence of an exact line from a file.
- `dybatpho::file_hash <string> [string]` — Print the checksum of a file.
- `dybatpho::file_size <string>` — Print the size of a file in bytes.
- `dybatpho::file_age_seconds <string>` — Print how many seconds have passed since a file was last modified.
- `dybatpho::file_backup <string>` — Copy a file next to itself under a timestamped name and print the copy's path, so that a caller can undo a change it is about to make.
- `dybatpho::find_up <string> [string]` — Search a directory and each of its parents for an entry, and print the first one found.
- `dybatpho::ensure_dir <string> [string]` — Create a directory and every missing parent, then print its path.
- `dybatpho::xdg_config_dir [string]` — Print the directory a program's configuration belongs in.
- `dybatpho::xdg_cache_dir [string]` — Print the directory a program's cache belongs in.
- `dybatpho::xdg_data_dir [string]` — Print the directory a program's data belongs in.
- `dybatpho::xdg_state_dir [string]` — Print the directory a program's state belongs in.
- `dybatpho::xdg_runtime_dir [string] [string]` — Print the directory a program's runtime files belong in: its sockets, named pipes, lock files and markers that must not outlive the login session.
- `dybatpho::file_mtime <string>` — Print when a file was last modified, as a Unix timestamp.
- `dybatpho::dir_size <string>` — Print the total size of the regular files in a directory tree.
- `dybatpho::file_is_binary <string>` — Return success when a file looks like binary rather than text.
- `dybatpho::create_temp_dir <string> [string] [string]` — Create a temporary directory and register it for cleanup on shell exit.

## forge

Utilities for talking to the forge a repository is hosted on. Loaded: `--modules forge`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/forge.md](docs/forge.md)

- `dybatpho::forge_host [string] [string]` — Print the host of the configured remote.
- `dybatpho::forge_kind [string] [string]` — Print which forge the repository is hosted on.
- `dybatpho::forge_repo [string] [string]` — Print the `owner/repo` the remote points at.
- `dybatpho::forge_api [string] [string]` — Print the API base URL for the repository's forge.
- `dybatpho::forge_token [string]` — Print the token used to authenticate against the forge.
- `dybatpho::forge_request <string> <string> [string] [string] <string...>` — Make an authenticated request against the forge API.
- `dybatpho::forge_error [string]` — Print what the forge said about the last failed request.
- `dybatpho::forge_issue_find <string>` — Print the number of an open issue whose title matches exactly.
- `dybatpho::forge_issue_create <string> <string> [string]` — Open an issue and print its number.
- `dybatpho::forge_issue_comment <string> <string>` — Add a comment to an existing issue.
- `dybatpho::forge_issue_report <string> <string> [string]` — Report something once, then keep reporting to the same issue.
- `dybatpho::forge_issue_url <string>` — Print the browser URL of an issue.
- `dybatpho::forge_release_find <string>` — Print the identifier of the release for a tag.
- `dybatpho::forge_release_create <string> [string] [string] [string]` — Create a release for a tag and print its identifier.
- `dybatpho::forge_release_upload <string> <string>` — Attach a file to an existing release and print its URL.

## git

Utilities for Git repositories. Loaded: `--modules git`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/git.md](docs/git.md)

- `dybatpho::git_root [string]` — Return the top-level directory of a Git repository.
- `dybatpho::git_common_dir [string]` — Print the absolute path of the Git directory a repository shares between its worktrees.
- `dybatpho::git_branch_exists <string> [string]` — Return success when a local branch exists.
- `dybatpho::git_branch [string]` — Return the current branch name, or a short SHA in detached HEAD state.
- `dybatpho::git_default_branch [string]` — Return the default branch of a Git repository.
- `dybatpho::git_commit_hash [string] [string]` — Return the full SHA of a commit.
- `dybatpho::git_commit_short_hash [string] [string]` — Return the short SHA of a commit.
- `dybatpho::git_commit_subject [string] [string]` — Return the subject line of a commit message.
- `dybatpho::git_commit_author [string] [string]` — Return the author name of a commit.
- `dybatpho::git_has_commit [string] [string]` — Return success when a commit exists.
- `dybatpho::git_commits_between <string> <string> [string]` — List commits reachable from a head ref but not from a base ref.
- `dybatpho::git_commit_count <string> <string> [string]` — Count commits in a range.
- `dybatpho::git_is_clean [string]` — Return success when the worktree has no tracked or untracked changes.
- `dybatpho::git_remote_url [string] [string]` — Return the URL for a Git remote.
- `dybatpho::git_has_remote [string] [string]` — Return success when a named remote exists.
- `dybatpho::git_changed_files [string] [string]` — List changed files relative to a base ref, including untracked.
- `dybatpho::git_latest_tag [string] [string]` — Print the highest version tag in a repository.
- `dybatpho::git_tags_containing [string] [string]` — List tags that contain a commit.
- `dybatpho::git_is_ancestor <string> <string> <string>` — Return success when one commit is reachable from another.
- `dybatpho::git_upstream [string] [string]` — Print the upstream a branch tracks.
- `dybatpho::git_ahead_behind [string] [string] [string]` — Count the commits a ref is ahead of and behind another.
- `dybatpho::git_state [string]` — Name the operation a repository is in the middle of.
- `dybatpho::git_is_shallow [string]` — Return success when a repository is a shallow clone.
- `dybatpho::git_stash_count [string]` — Count the entries on the stash.
- `dybatpho::git_worktree_list [string]` — List the worktrees of a repository with the branch each has checked out.

## helpers

Utilities for common shell-script helper patterns.. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/helpers.md](docs/helpers.md)

- `dybatpho::expect_args <string...>` — Validate function arguments and assign them into named local variables.
- `dybatpho::expect_ref <string>` — Check that a caller-supplied variable name can safely be bound to a nameref, and stop the script when it cannot.
- `dybatpho::still_has_args` — Check whether at least one more positional argument remains after the current one.
- `dybatpho::expect_envs <string...>` — Ensure that required environment variables are set.
- `dybatpho::require <string> <string> [number]` — Ensure that a required command is installed, and new enough.
- `dybatpho::has_version <string>` — Tell whether a command is installed, and new enough, without stopping the script: the question `dybatpho::require` asks, for a caller that wants to take another path rather than stop.
- `dybatpho::command_exists_all <string...>` — Return success when all listed commands are available.
- `dybatpho::is <string> <string>` — Check whether a value matches a supported shell-oriented condition.
- `dybatpho::coalesce <string...>` — Print the first non-empty value from a list of fallbacks.
- `dybatpho::coalesce_cmd <string...>` — Print the first available command from a list of candidates.
- `dybatpho::default_env <string> <string>` — Assign and export a default value for an environment variable when it is empty.
- `dybatpho::require_envs_any <string...>` — Ensure that at least one of the listed environment variables is set.
- `dybatpho::assert [string] [string]` — Run a check and stop with a message when it fails.
- `dybatpho::retry <number> [string] <string...>` — Retry a command with escalating delays until it succeeds or retries are exhausted.
- `dybatpho::retry_until <number> <number> [string] <string...>` — Retry a command until it succeeds or the retry budget is exhausted, using a fixed delay.
- `dybatpho::breakpoint` — Open an interactive breakpoint for debugging a running script.
- `dybatpho::provides <string> <string...>` — Print the module that defines a function.
- `dybatpho::describe <string>` — Print the documentation comment of a function.
- `dybatpho::function_list [string]` — Print the public functions this shell has loaded.

## i18n

Utilities for translating messages and formatting values for a locale. Loaded: `--modules i18n`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/i18n.md](docs/i18n.md)

- `dybatpho::i18n_reset` — Forget every loaded catalog, the resolved locale, and the recorded misses.
- `dybatpho::i18n_locale` — Print the locale currently in effect, resolving it on first use.
- `dybatpho::i18n_set_locale <string>` — Use a locale for every later translation and formatting call.
- `dybatpho::i18n_chain [string]` — Print the fallback chain a lookup walks for a locale, most specific first.
- `dybatpho::i18n_plural_form <number> [string]` — Print the CLDR plural category a count takes in a language.
- `dybatpho::i18n_t <string> <string...>` — Translate a message and fill in its placeholders.
- `dybatpho::i18n_tn <string> <number> <string...>` — Translate a message, choosing the plural form the count takes in the target language.
- `dybatpho::i18n_tc <string> <string> <string...>` — Translate a message that is qualified by a context, so that one English word with two meanings can be translated two ways.
- `dybatpho::i18n_has <string>` — Report whether a key has a translation, without recording a miss and without rendering anything.
- `dybatpho::i18n_missing` — Print every key that was looked up and not found in this shell.
- `dybatpho::i18n_library_message <string>` — Translate a diagnostic that dybatpho itself emitted.
- `dybatpho::i18n_library_text <string> <string> <string...>` — Translate a piece of dybatpho's own user interface that carries a value.
- `dybatpho::i18n_library_plural <string> <number> <string> <string...>` — Translate a piece of dybatpho's own user interface that counts something, choosing the plural form the count takes in the target language.
- `dybatpho::i18n_number <string> [number] [string]` — Format a number the way a locale writes it.
- `dybatpho::i18n_number_plain <string> [number]` — Format a number without grouping and with a dot decimal mark, whatever the locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_percent <string> [number] [string]` — Format a value as a percentage the way a locale writes it.
- `dybatpho::i18n_currency <string> <string> [string]` — Format a monetary amount for a locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_bytes <number> [string] [string]` — Format a byte count for people, grouping the digits for the locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_month_name <number> [string] [string]` — Print the name of a month in a locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_weekday_name <number> [string] [string]` — Print the name of a weekday in a locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_date <number> [string] [string]` — Format a timestamp as a date the way a locale writes it.
- `dybatpho::i18n_time <number> [string] [string]` — Format a timestamp as a time of day the way a locale writes it, including whether it uses a 12-hour or a 24-hour clock.
- `dybatpho::i18n_datetime <number> [string] [string]` — Format a timestamp as a date and time together.
- `dybatpho::i18n_date_pattern <number> <string> [string]` — Format a timestamp against an explicit pattern.
- `dybatpho::i18n_relative <number> [number] [string]` — Describe when a timestamp happened relative to another one.
- `dybatpho::i18n_duration <number> [string]` — Describe a span of time without saying whether it is past or future.
- `dybatpho::i18n_is_rtl [string]` — Report whether a locale is written right to left.
- `dybatpho::i18n_direction [string]` — Print the direction a locale is written in.
- `dybatpho::i18n_bidi_mark <string>` — Print a bidirectional mark, which forces the direction of the text around it without being visible itself.
- `dybatpho::i18n_bidi_isolate <string> [string]` — Wrap text so that its direction cannot leak into the text around it.
- `dybatpho::i18n_bidi_strip <string>` — Remove every bidirectional control character from text, so that it can be compared or measured.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_number <string> <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Add or replace the number symbols of a locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_currency <string> <string> <number>` — Add or replace a currency's symbol and decimal digits.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_currency_layout <string> <string>` — Set where a locale puts a currency symbol.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_date <string> <string> <string>` — Add or replace one date or time pattern of a locale.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_names <string> <string> <string>` — Add or replace a locale's month, weekday, or day period names.
- `dybatpho::i18n_register_rtl <string...>` — Record additional languages as being written right to left.
- `dybatpho::i18n_load <string> [string] [string]` — Load message catalogs.
- `dybatpho::i18n_init [string] [string]` — Resolve the locale and load its catalogs, once.
- `dybatpho::i18n_locales [string]` — Print the locales that have a catalog somewhere on the search path.
- `dybatpho::i18n_extract <string> <string...>` — Write a catalog template covering every key a source tree refers to, so a translator has something to fill in rather than a blank file.
- `dybatpho::i18n_lint <string> <string...>` — Compare a locale's catalog against a reference one and report what a translator still has to do.

## json

Utilities for working with JSON and YAML data. Loaded: `--modules json`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/json.md](docs/json.md)

- `dybatpho::json_query <string> <string> <string...>` — Query a JSON document with a `jq` filter.
- `dybatpho::json_has <string> <string>` — Return success when a JSON document satisfies a `jq` filter.
- `dybatpho::json_pretty <string> [string]` — Pretty-print a JSON document.
- `dybatpho::json_to_yaml <string> [string]` — Convert a JSON document to YAML.
- `dybatpho::yaml_query <string> <string> <string...>` — Query a YAML document with a `jq` filter.
- `dybatpho::yaml_has <string> <string>` — Return success when a YAML document satisfies a `jq` filter.
- `dybatpho::yaml_pretty <string> [string]` — Pretty-print a YAML document.
- `dybatpho::yaml_to_json <string> [string]` — Convert a YAML document to JSON.
- `dybatpho::json_string <string>` — Encode a string as a JSON string value, surrounding quotes included.
- `dybatpho::json_object <string...>` — Build a JSON object from name and value pairs.
- `dybatpho::json_eval <string> <string>` — Evaluate a `jq` filter against a JSON document held in a variable.
- `dybatpho::json_get <string> <string>` — Evaluate a `jq` filter and print the result as a bare scalar.
- `dybatpho::json_valid <string>` — Return success when a JSON document held in a variable is valid.
- `dybatpho::json_set [string] <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Set the value at a path in a JSON document.
- `dybatpho::json_del <string> <string> [string]` — Remove the value at a path from a JSON document.
- `dybatpho::json_merge <string> <string> [string]` — Deep-merge two JSON objects, the overlay winning.
- `dybatpho::yaml_set [string] <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Set the value at a path in a YAML document.
- `dybatpho::yaml_del <string> <string> [string]` — Remove the value at a path from a YAML document.
- `dybatpho::yaml_merge <string> <string> [string]` — Deep-merge two YAML mappings, the overlay winning.

## lock

Utilities for process locking and coordination. Loaded: `--modules lock`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/lock.md](docs/lock.md)

- `dybatpho::lock_hostname` — Print the host name a lock records as its owner.
- `dybatpho::lock_path <string>` — Resolve a lock name or path into an absolute lock directory path.
- `dybatpho::lock_field <string> <string>` — Read a single metadata field recorded for a lock.
- `dybatpho::lock_is_alive <string>` — Return success when the process that owns a lock is still alive on this host.
- `dybatpho::lock_is_held <string>` — Return success when a lock is currently held by a live process.
- `dybatpho::lock_info <string>` — Print information about the process currently holding a lock.
- `dybatpho::lock_reclaim_stale <string>` — Remove a lock left behind by a process that is no longer running.
- `dybatpho::lock_acquire <string> [number]` — Acquire a portable, cross-platform (Linux/macOS) file lock, waiting up to a timeout.
- `dybatpho::lock_release <string>` — Release a lock previously acquired by the current process.
- `dybatpho::with_lock <string> <number> <string> <string...>` — Acquire a lock, run a command while holding it, then release it, even if the command fails.
- `dybatpho::flock_acquire <string> <path> [number]` — Take a `flock` on a file through a descriptor of its own, for sharing a lock with other programs that `flock` the same file.
- `dybatpho::flock_release <number>` — Let go of a lock taken by `dybatpho::flock_acquire` and close its descriptor.
- `dybatpho::with_flock <path> <number> <string> <string...>` — Take a `flock` on a file, run a command while holding it, then let go, even if the command fails.
- `dybatpho::lock_semaphore_acquire <string> <number> [number] [string]` — Take one of a fixed number of slots, so that at most that many processes run a section at once, waiting up to a timeout for one to free up.
- `dybatpho::lock_semaphore_release <string> <number> [number]` — Give back a semaphore slot taken by the current process.
- `dybatpho::lock_semaphore_holders <string> <number>` — Print who holds each taken slot of a semaphore.
- `dybatpho::with_semaphore <string> <number> <number> <string> <string...>` — Take a semaphore slot, run a command while holding it, then give the slot back, even if the command fails or the shell is interrupted.

## logging

Utilities for logging to stdout/stderr. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/logging.md](docs/logging.md)

- `dybatpho::compare_log_level <string> [string]` — Return success when a message level should be shown against a threshold.
- `dybatpho::validate_log_level <string>` — Validate a candidate log level value.
- `dybatpho::debug <string>` — Show debug message.
- `dybatpho::debug_command <string> <string> <string...>` — Log a debug message together with the output of a command.
- `dybatpho::info <string>` — Show info message.
- `dybatpho::print <string>` — Show normal message.
- `dybatpho::progress <string>` — Show a highlighted in-progress banner.
- `dybatpho::progress_bar <number> [number]` — Render a percentage-based progress bar on the current output line.
- `dybatpho::header <string>` — Show a section header banner.
- `dybatpho::success <string>` — Show success message.
- `dybatpho::warn <string>` — Show warning message.
- `dybatpho::error <string>` — Show error message.
- `dybatpho::fatal <string> <number>` — Show fatal message.
- `dybatpho::log_to_file <string> [string...]` — Send structured JSON events to a file alongside the human-readable output on stderr, and keep that file bounded by rotating it.
- `dybatpho::log_context <string> <string...>` — Attach fields to every structured log event that follows, so a run identifier or a stage name rides along with each JSON line instead of being spelled out in every message.
- `dybatpho::timer_start <string>` — Start a named timer whose elapsed time `dybatpho::timer_end` logs.
- `dybatpho::timer_end <string> [string]` — Stop a named timer and log how long it ran.
- `dybatpho::spinner <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command while a spinner reports that it is still going, then pass its exit code back unchanged.
- `dybatpho::start_trace` — Enable Bash tracing with dybatpho formatting.
- `dybatpho::end_trace` — Disable Bash tracing started by `dybatpho::start_trace`.
