- `dybatpho::md_raw <string>` — Mark text as Markdown that is already formatted, so a builder embeds it instead of escaping it.
- `dybatpho::md_escape <string>` — Escape the Markdown-significant characters in a text block.
- `dybatpho::md_heading <number> <string>` — Render an ATX heading.
- `dybatpho::md_list <string> [string]` — Render a bullet or ordered list, one item per input line.
- `dybatpho::md_task_list <string> [string]` — Render a GitHub-flavored task list, one item per input line.
- `dybatpho::md_link <string> <string> [string]` — Render an inline link.
- `dybatpho::md_badge <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Render a shields.io badge as an image, optionally wrapped in a link.
- `dybatpho::md_code_block <string> <string>` — Render a fenced code block.
- `dybatpho::md_table <string> [string]` — Render a Markdown table through `table.sh`.
- `dybatpho::md_collapsible <string> <string>` — Render a collapsible `<details>` section.
- `dybatpho::md_mention <string>` — Render a mention of a user or group.
- `dybatpho::md_emoji <string>` — Render an emoji shortcode.

## math

Exact decimal arithmetic, comparison, rounding and aggregation. Loaded: `--modules math`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/math.md](docs/math.md)

- `dybatpho::math_is_number <string>` — Return success when a value is a plain decimal number.
- `dybatpho::math_is_integer <string>` — Return success when a value is a whole number.
- `dybatpho::math_add <string...>` — Add numbers exactly.
- `dybatpho::math_sub <string...>` — Subtract the second number from the first, and any further numbers from the running result.
- `dybatpho::math_mul <string...>` — Multiply numbers exactly.
- `dybatpho::math_div <string> <string> [number]` — Divide one number by another, rounding half away from zero.
- `dybatpho::math_mod <string> <string>` — Print the remainder of an integer division.
- `dybatpho::math_pow <string> <string> [number]` — Raise a number to a whole power.
- `dybatpho::math_abs <string>` — Print a number without its sign.
- `dybatpho::math_neg <string>` — Print a number with its sign flipped.
- `dybatpho::math_compare <string> <string>` — Compare two numbers by value rather than as strings.
- `dybatpho::math_gt <string> <string>` — Return success when the first number is greater than the second.
- `dybatpho::math_lt <string> <string>` — Return success when the first number is less than the second.
- `dybatpho::math_eq <string> <string>` — Return success when two numbers have the same value, whatever their spelling: `2.50`, `2.5` and `+2.5` are all equal.
- `dybatpho::math_trunc <string>` — Truncate toward zero, dropping the fractional part.
- `dybatpho::math_floor <string>` — Round down, toward negative infinity.
- `dybatpho::math_ceil <string>` — Round up, toward positive infinity.
- `dybatpho::math_round <string> [number]` — Round to a number of fraction digits, halves away from zero.
- `dybatpho::math_add_into <string> <string...>` — Add numbers exactly, into a named variable.
- `dybatpho::math_sub_into <string> <string...>` — Subtract numbers exactly, into a named variable: the second from the first, and any further ones from the running result, as `dybatpho::math_sub` does.
- `dybatpho::math_mul_into <string> <string...>` — Multiply numbers exactly, into a named variable, as `dybatpho::math_mul` does.
- `dybatpho::math_div_into <string> <string> <string> [number]` — Divide one number by another into a named variable, rounding half away from zero, as `dybatpho::math_div` does.
- `dybatpho::math_compare_into <string> <string> <string>` — Compare two numbers by value into a named variable, as `dybatpho::math_compare` does: `-1`, `0` or `1`.
- `dybatpho::math_round_into <string> <string> [number]` — Round to a number of fraction digits into a named variable, halves away from zero, as `dybatpho::math_round` does.
- `dybatpho::math_min <string...>` — Print the smallest of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_max <string...>` — Print the largest of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_sum <string...>` — Add up a list of numbers exactly.
- `dybatpho::math_avg <string...>` — Print the mean of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_median <string...>` — Print the median of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_percentile <string> <string...>` — Print a percentile of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_sqrt <string> [number]` — Print the square root of a number.
- `dybatpho::math_stddev [options] <string...>` — Print the standard deviation of a list of numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_clamp <string> <string> <string>` — Hold a number inside a range.
- `dybatpho::math_percent <string> <string> [number]` — Print what percentage one number is of another.
- `dybatpho::math_gcd <string...>` — Print the greatest common divisor of whole numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_lcm <string...>` — Print the least common multiple of whole numbers.
- `dybatpho::math_random <string> <string>` — Print a random whole number in an inclusive range.

## metrics

Utilities for measuring a script and exporting the result to Prometheus. Loaded: `--modules metrics`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/metrics.md](docs/metrics.md)

- `dybatpho::metrics_help <string> <string>` — Describe a metric, so that the exported text explains it.
- `dybatpho::metrics_counter_inc <string> [number] <string...>` — Add to a counter, a value that only ever grows.
- `dybatpho::metrics_gauge_set <string> <number> <string...>` — Set a gauge, a value that can go up and down.
- `dybatpho::metrics_observe_ms <string> <number> <string...>` — Record one duration in a histogram.
- `dybatpho::metrics_summary_ms <string> <number> <string...>` — Record one duration in a summary, which exports quantiles.
- `dybatpho::metrics_timer_start <string>` — Start a named timer.
- `dybatpho::metrics_timer_stop <string> <string...>` — Stop a timer, record its duration, and print the elapsed milliseconds.
- `dybatpho::metrics_time <string> <string...>` — Run a command, record how long it took, and pass its exit code on.
- `dybatpho::metrics_get <string> <string> <string...>` — Read one series back, for a script that branches on its own measurements and for tests.
- `dybatpho::metrics_reset` — Forget every recorded metric.
- `dybatpho::metrics_render` — Render every recorded metric in the Prometheus text exposition format.
- `dybatpho::metrics_write <string>` — Write the rendered metrics to a file, atomically.
- `dybatpho::metrics_push [options] <string> <string> <string...>` — Push the recorded metrics to a Prometheus Pushgateway.

## network

Utilities for network. Loaded: `--modules network`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/network.md](docs/network.md)

- `dybatpho::curl_do <string> [string] <string>` — Transferring data with URL by curl
- `dybatpho::curl_download <string> <string> <string...>` — Download file
- `dybatpho::curl_json <string> [string] <string...>` — Transfer JSON data with URL by curl.
- `dybatpho::curl_head <string> [string] <string...>` — Fetch only HTTP headers for a URL by curl.
- `dybatpho::curl_upload <string> [string] <string...>` — Upload fields and files with curl using multipart/form-data.
- `dybatpho::verify_checksum <string> <string>` — Verify a downloaded file against an expected checksum.
- `dybatpho::curl_resume_download <string> <string> [string] <string...>` — Download a file with resume support and optional checksum verification.
- `dybatpho::curl_parse_response <string> [string]` — Parse a raw curl header dump (and optional body file) into normalized response state.
- `dybatpho::curl_response_header <string> [string]` — Print a normalized response header captured by `dybatpho::curl_parse_response`.
- `dybatpho::curl_request <string> [string] <string...>` — Perform a request via `dybatpho::curl_do` and parse its response into normalized status/header/body state.
- `dybatpho::curl_timeout <string> [string] [number] [number] <string...>` — Perform a request via `dybatpho::curl_do` with connect/total timeouts scoped to this call only.
- `dybatpho::circuit_state <string>` — Report whether a circuit breaker key is currently open, half-open, or closed.
- `dybatpho::circuit_reset <string>` — Reset a circuit breaker key back to the closed state.
- `dybatpho::circuit_breaker <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command guarded by a circuit breaker keyed by name.
- `dybatpho::rate_limit_remaining <string> <string>` — Report how many calls a rate limit key has left in its window.
- `dybatpho::rate_limit_reset <string>` — Forget every call recorded against a rate limit key.
- `dybatpho::rate_limit <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command under a sliding window rate limit keyed by name.
- `dybatpho::curl_link <string>` — Print the URL of one relation of the last response's `Link` header.
- `dybatpho::curl_paginate <string> <string...>` — Fetch every page of a paginated resource, following the `Link` header's `next` relation, and print each page's body to standard output.
- `dybatpho::curl_auth_bearer <string> <string> [string] <string...>` — Make a request carrying a bearer token, without putting the token on `curl`'s command line.
- `dybatpho::curl_graphql <string> <string> [string] [string] <string...>` — Post a GraphQL query and report the errors the response carries.
- `dybatpho::url_parse <string>` — Split a URL into its components.
- `dybatpho::url_part <string> [string]` — Print one component of the last parsed URL.
- `dybatpho::is_ipv4 <string>` — Return success when a value is an IPv4 address.
- `dybatpho::is_ipv6 <string>` — Return success when a value is an IPv6 address.
- `dybatpho::ip_version <string>` — Print which version of IP an address is.
- `dybatpho::is_cidr <string>` — Return success when a value is a CIDR block.
- `dybatpho::cidr_netmask <string>` — Print the dotted-decimal subnet mask of an IPv4 prefix length.
- `dybatpho::cidr_contains <string> <string>` — Return success when an address falls inside a CIDR block.
- `dybatpho::port_open <string> <number> [number]` — Return success when a TCP port accepts a connection.
- `dybatpho::wait_port <string> <number> [number] [number]` — Wait until a TCP port accepts a connection.

## notification

Utilities for sending messages to chat and notification providers. Loaded: `--modules notification`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/notification.md](docs/notification.md)

- `dybatpho::notify_slack <string>` — Send a message to a Slack channel via Incoming Webhook.
- `dybatpho::notify_telegram <string> [string]` — Send a message to a Telegram chat via Bot API.
- `dybatpho::notify_teams <string> [string]` — Send a message to a Microsoft Teams channel via Incoming Webhook.
- `dybatpho::notify_google_chat <string>` — Send a message to a Google Chat space via Incoming Webhook.
- `dybatpho::notify_discord <string> [string]` — Send a message to a Discord channel via Incoming Webhook.
- `dybatpho::notify_webhook <string> <string> <string...>` — Send a raw JSON payload to an arbitrary webhook URL via HTTP POST.
- `dybatpho::notify_desktop <string> [string] [string]` — Show a notification on the local desktop.
- `dybatpho::notify_ntfy <string> [string] [string] [string]` — Publish a message to an [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) topic, on ntfy.sh or a server of your own.
- `dybatpho::notify_gotify <string> [string] [string]` — Push a message to a [Gotify](https://gotify.net) server.
- `dybatpho::notify_email <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Send a plain-text email through the local `sendmail`.

## os

Utilities for getting information of OS/distro. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/os.md](docs/os.md)

- `dybatpho::goos` — Get $GOOS compilation environment
- `dybatpho::platform` — Return the normalized host operating system name.
- `dybatpho::is_macos` — Return success when running on macOS.
- `dybatpho::is_linux` — Return success when running on Linux.
- `dybatpho::is_windows` — Return success when running on a Windows-compatible environment such as Cygwin, MSYS, or MinGW.
- `dybatpho::command_path <string...>` — Return the path of the first installed command.
- `dybatpho::command_version <string>` — Print the version a command reports.
- `dybatpho::goarch` — Get $GOARCH compilation environment
- `dybatpho::hostname` — Print the host name of the machine.
- `dybatpho::user` — Print the name of the user the script runs as.
- `dybatpho::is_root` — Return success when the script runs as the superuser.
- `dybatpho::kernel_version` — Print the kernel release of the host.
- `dybatpho::cpu_count` — Print how many processors the host can run work on.
- `dybatpho::is_tty [string]` — Return success when a standard stream is attached to a terminal.
- `dybatpho::color_supported [string]` — Return success when output on a stream should carry ANSI colour.
- `dybatpho::terminal_width [number]` — Print the width of the terminal in columns.
- `dybatpho::terminal_height [number]` — Print the height of the terminal in lines.
- `dybatpho::os_release <string>` — Print one field of the host's `os-release` file.
- `dybatpho::distro` — Print the distribution the host runs.
- `dybatpho::distro_version` — Print the version of the distribution the host runs.
- `dybatpho::is_container` — Return success when the script runs inside a container.
- `dybatpho::is_wsl` — Return success when the script runs under the Windows Subsystem for Linux.
- `dybatpho::is_ci` — Return success when the script runs on a continuous integration service.

## parallel

Utilities for running work concurrently with a bounded worker pool. Loaded: `--modules parallel`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/parallel.md](docs/parallel.md)

- `dybatpho::parallel_map [options] <number> <string> <string...>` — Run one command once per item, several items at a time.
- `dybatpho::parallel_run [options] <number> <string...>` — Run several commands at once.
- `dybatpho::parallel_status <number>` — Print the exit code of one job of the last run.
- `dybatpho::parallel_count` — Print how many jobs the last run had.
- `dybatpho::parallel_failed` — Print how many jobs of the last run failed.

## pkg

Package manager detection and guarded dependency installation. Loaded: `--modules pkg`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/pkg.md](docs/pkg.md)

- `dybatpho::pkg_supported` — Print every package manager this module supports.
- `dybatpho::pkg_manager` — Report the package manager of the current machine.
- `dybatpho::pkg_manager_available [string]` — Return success when a package manager is usable on this machine.
- `dybatpho::pkg_name <string> [string...]` — Resolve a package name for the current manager from `<manager>:<package>` overrides.
- `dybatpho::pkg_installed <string>` — Return success when a package is installed, according to the detected manager.
- `dybatpho::pkg_missing <string...>` — Print the packages that are not installed yet.
- `dybatpho::pkg_install_command <string> <string...>` — Print the command that would install the given packages, without running it.
- `dybatpho::pkg_update <string>` — Refresh the package index, after confirming the change.
- `dybatpho::pkg_install <string> <string...>` — Install packages with the detected manager, after confirming the change.
- `dybatpho::pkg_ensure <string> <string...>` — Install only the packages that are missing, and do nothing when they are all there.
- `dybatpho::pkg_require <string> <string> [string...]` — Make sure a command is available, installing the package that provides it on this machine.

## privilege

Acquiring and holding a privilege escalation for a run. Loaded: `--modules privilege`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/privilege.md](docs/privilege.md)

- `dybatpho::privilege_command` — Print the escalation command this host should use.
- `dybatpho::privilege_needed` — Return success when a command has to be elevated to run.
- `dybatpho::privilege_acquire [options] <string>` — Authenticate once and hold the escalation for this run.
- `dybatpho::privilege_release` — Let the escalation go: stop the refresher and take the wrapper off `PATH`.
- `dybatpho::privilege_run <string> <string...>` — Run one command elevated, for a caller that needs that and no session.

## process

Utilities for process handling. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/process.md](docs/process.md)

- `dybatpho::die <string> [number]` — Log a fatal message and stop the current script or process.
- `dybatpho::register_err_handler` — Register the ERR trap handler used by dybatpho scripts.
- `dybatpho::register_killed_handler` — Register handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM.
- `dybatpho::register_common_handlers` — Register both error and signal handlers.
- `dybatpho::run_err_handler <number>` — Handle a command failure captured by `dybatpho::register_err_handler`.
- `dybatpho::killed_process_handler <string>` — Handle SIGINT or SIGTERM received by the current process.
- `dybatpho::trap <string> <string...>` — Append a command to one or more trap handlers without discarding existing traps.
- `dybatpho::cleanup_file_on_exit <string>` — Register a file or directory to be removed when the current shell exits.
- `dybatpho::dry_run <string...>` — Print a command instead of executing it when dry-run mode is enabled.
- `dybatpho::try <string> <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command and catch its failure, including a `dybatpho::die` or an `exit`, instead of letting it end the script.
- `dybatpho::run_with_timeout <number> <string...>` — Run a command and end it if it takes too long.
- `dybatpho::background_run <string> <string...>` — Start a command in the background under a name.
- `dybatpho::background_pid <string>` — Print the process ID of a background job.
- `dybatpho::background_status <string>` — Print the exit code of a background job that has finished.
- `dybatpho::wait_all` — Wait for every background job started by `dybatpho::background_run`.
- `dybatpho::kill_children` — End every background job started by `dybatpho::background_run`, together with the processes those jobs started.
- `dybatpho::pid_file_write <string> [number]` — Write a process ID to a PID file.
- `dybatpho::pid_file_is_running <string>` — Report whether the process recorded in a PID file is still alive.
- `dybatpho::pid_file_remove <string> [number]` — Remove a PID file, but only when it records the given process.

## profile

Utilities for finding where a Bash script spends its time. Loaded: `--modules profile`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/profile.md](docs/profile.md)

- `dybatpho::profile_begin <string>` — Start timing a block.
- `dybatpho::profile_end <string>` — Stop timing the innermost open block, which must be the one named.
- `dybatpho::profile_run <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command inside a block, ending the block whatever the command returns.
- `dybatpho::profile_start` — Time every function from now on, each as a block of its name, until `dybatpho::profile_stop`.
- `dybatpho::profile_stop` — Stop timing every function, end the blocks it opened, and put back the `functrace` setting the caller had and its `DEBUG` trap.
- `dybatpho::profile_report <string>` — Print the recorded blocks: name, calls, total and self time in milliseconds, the most self time first, then by name.
- `dybatpho::profile_reset` — Forget every recorded block and every open one.

## queue

A durable job queue backed by the filesystem. Loaded: `--modules queue`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/queue.md](docs/queue.md)

- `dybatpho::queue_push [options] <string> <string>` — Add a job to a queue.
- `dybatpho::queue_pop <string> <string> <string>` — Claim the next job in a queue: the oldest of the highest priority among the jobs that are due.
- `dybatpho::queue_peek <string> [string]` — Read the job a claim would take next, without claiming it.
- `dybatpho::queue_len <string> [string]` — Count the jobs in one of a queue's states.
- `dybatpho::queue_list <string> [string]` — List a queue's job ids for one state, oldest first.
- `dybatpho::queue_complete <string> <string>` — Remove a claimed job, marking the work as done.
- `dybatpho::queue_requeue [options] <string> <string> [number]` — Put a claimed job back at the end of the queue.
- `dybatpho::queue_dead_letter <string> <string>` — Move a claimed job to the queue's dead letters.
- `dybatpho::queue_read <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Read a job's payload from any state, into a named variable.
- `dybatpho::queue_work [options] <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a worker over a queue: claim each job that is due, hand its payload to a handler, and settle the job by how the handler exited.

## release

Utilities for cutting a release from a Git repository. Loaded: `--modules release`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/release.md](docs/release.md)

- `dybatpho::release_commit_parse <string> [string]` — Break a commit message into the parts Conventional Commits defines.
- `dybatpho::release_commit_type <string>` — Classify one commit subject as Conventional Commits does.
- `dybatpho::release_bump_type <string> <string> [string]` — Decide how far the version should move, from the commits in a range.
- `dybatpho::release_next_version [string] [string] [string]` — Print the version a release from these commits should carry.
- `dybatpho::release_changelog <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Render the changelog entry for a range of commits.
- `dybatpho::release_artifact_name <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Print the name a release artifact should carry for one platform.
- `dybatpho::release_package <string> <string> <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Package build output into a release artifact for one platform.
- `dybatpho::release_checksums <string> [string]` — Write one checksum file covering every artifact in a directory.
- `dybatpho::release_sign <string> [string]` — Sign a file and print the signature's path.

## safety

Guards for destructive operations. Loaded: `--modules safety`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/safety.md](docs/safety.md)

- `dybatpho::is_interactive` — Return success when the script can ask the user a question.
- `dybatpho::confirm <string> [string]` — Ask a yes/no question and return the answer as an exit code.
- `dybatpho::assert_safe_path <string> [string]` — Validate a path before a destructive operation and print it as an absolute path.
- `dybatpho::safe_rm <string> <string...>` — Remove files and directories after validating them and confirming the removal.
- `dybatpho::safe_overwrite <string> <string>` — Confirm that an existing file may be replaced, optionally keeping a backup.
- `dybatpho::safe_copy <string> <string> <string>` — Copy a file or directory, guarding the destination against an accidental overwrite.
- `dybatpho::safe_move <string> <string> <string>` — Move a file or directory, guarding the destination against an accidental overwrite.
- `dybatpho::safe_extract <string> <string> [string] [number]` — Extract an archive after rejecting entries that escape the destination.
- `dybatpho::safe_system <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command that changes system state, after confirming it.

## schedule

Deciding when a command should run, and running it on a cadence. Loaded: `--modules schedule`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/schedule.md](docs/schedule.md)

- `dybatpho::schedule_every [options] <number> <string> <string...>` — Run a command on a fixed cadence until it is interrupted.
- `dybatpho::schedule_debounce <number> <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command once a burst of triggers has settled.
- `dybatpho::schedule_once_per <string> <string> <string> <string...>` — Run a command at most once in each period.
- `dybatpho::schedule_reset <string>` — Forget what a key has recorded, so the next call runs.
- `dybatpho::schedule_cron_due <string> [number]` — Return success when a time matches a cron expression.

## screen

Full-screen terminal applications: layout, widgets, and an event loop. Loaded: `--modules screen`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/screen.md](docs/screen.md)

- `dybatpho::screen_width <string> <string>` — Return the number of terminal columns a string occupies.
- `dybatpho::screen_put <number> <number> <string> [string]` — Draw text into the buffer at one position, clipped to the screen.
- `dybatpho::screen_clear` — Reset the buffer to blank, which is where every frame starts.
- `dybatpho::screen_size` — Resize the buffer to the terminal, and report whether it changed.
- `dybatpho::screen_flush` — Write the rows that changed since the last frame to the terminal.
- `dybatpho::screen_rect <string> <number> <number> <number> <number>` — Build a rectangle from its parts.
- `dybatpho::screen_layout <string> <string> <string> <string...>` — Split a rectangle into parts that satisfy a list of constraints.
- `dybatpho::screen_rect_inner <string> <string> [number]` — Shrink a rectangle by a margin on every side.
- `dybatpho::screen_rect_center <string> <string> <number> <number>` — Centre a rectangle of a given size inside another, which is what a popup needs.
- `dybatpho::screen_begin` — Take over the terminal: alternate screen, raw mode, hidden cursor, and mouse reporting.
- `dybatpho::screen_end` — Give the terminal back: mouse reporting off, cursor shown, the alternate screen left, the original line settings restored, and the caller's INT, TERM and WINCH handlers put back.
- `dybatpho::screen_event <string> [string]` — Wait for the next event and report it under a stable name.
- `dybatpho::screen_pending` — Return success when an event is already waiting, so reading it with `dybatpho::screen_event` will not block.
- `dybatpho::screen_block <string> <string...>` — Draw a bordered box, optionally titled, and report the area left inside it.
- `dybatpho::screen_text <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw text in a rectangle, wrapped and aligned.
- `dybatpho::screen_list <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw a scrollable list of items with one of them selected.
- `dybatpho::screen_table <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw a table with a header and an optional selected row.
- `dybatpho::screen_gauge <string> <number> <number> <string...>` — Draw a horizontal gauge filled to a ratio, with a label centred on it.
- `dybatpho::screen_tabs <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw a row of tabs with one of them active.
- `dybatpho::screen_scrollbar <string> <number> <number> <string...>` — Draw a vertical scrollbar showing where a window sits in a list longer than the screen.
- `dybatpho::screen_sparkline <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw a one-row sparkline from a series of numbers.
- `dybatpho::screen_barchart <string> <string> <string...>` — Draw horizontal bars, one per value, with optional labels.
- `dybatpho::screen_chart <string> <string> <string...>` — Plot a series as a line chart, using Braille dots for a resolution of two points across and four down inside every character.
- `dybatpho::screen_popup <string> <string...>` — Blank a rectangle and draw a block over it, which is what a dialog or a menu laid over the screen needs.
- `dybatpho::screen_spans <number> <number> <number> <string> <string...>` — Draw pieces of text side by side on one row, each in its own style, cut to a width.
- `dybatpho::screen_ansi <number> <number> <number> <string>` — Draw a line that carries its own SGR colour sequences -- the output of a command, a log written by another program -- keeping its colours.
- `dybatpho::screen_keybar <string> <string...>` — Draw a one-row bar of key hints: each key in `DYBATPHO_SCREEN_STYLE_KEY`, what it does after it, all over `DYBATPHO_SCREEN_STYLE_KEYBAR` across the whole width.
- `dybatpho::screen_theme <string>` — Set every `DYBATPHO_SCREEN_STYLE_*` variable from a named palette, so an application gets a consistent look without choosing a colour for each widget.

## secret

Utilities for handling secrets safely. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/secret.md](docs/secret.md)

- `dybatpho::secret_register <string...>` — Register secret values so they are masked in logs, errors, and masked output.
- `dybatpho::secret_forget` — Forget every registered secret so masking stops.
- `dybatpho::secret_mask [string...]` — Mask registered secrets in arguments or in stdin.
- `dybatpho::secret_mask_run <string...>` — Run a command and mask registered secrets in its output.
- `dybatpho::secret_hint <string> [number]` — Print a non-reversible hint for a secret, revealing only its last characters.
- `dybatpho::secret_check_permission <string> [string]` — Verify that a secret file is owned by the current user and isn't readable by others.
- `dybatpho::secret_from_file <string> <string>` — Read a secret from a file into a variable and register it for masking.
- `dybatpho::secret_from_env <string> <string> <string>` — Read a secret from an environment variable and unset the source variable.
- `dybatpho::secret_from_stdin <string> [string]` — Read a secret from stdin, without echoing it when the input is a terminal.
- `dybatpho::secret_read <string> <string> [string]` — Read a secret from a source specification.
- `dybatpho::secret_write_file <string> <string>` — Write a secret to a file that only its owner can read.
- `dybatpho::secret_with_file <string> <string...>` — Run a command that needs the secret as a file, without writing it to disk.
- `dybatpho::secret_no_history` — Stop the current shell from recording commands into a history file.
- `dybatpho::secret_wipe <string...>` — Overwrite and unset variables that hold secrets.
- `dybatpho::secret_shred <string...>` — Remove files containing secrets, overwriting their content when possible.

## semver

Utilities for working with Semantic Versioning (semver). Loaded: `--modules semver`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/semver.md](docs/semver.md)

- `dybatpho::semver_valid <string>` — Return success when the string is a valid semver (with optional leading v).
- `dybatpho::semver_parse <string>` — Parse a semver string and print its components, one per line.
- `dybatpho::semver_compare <string> <string>` — Compare two semver strings according to semver 2.0.0 precedence rules.
- `dybatpho::semver_bump <string> <string> [string] [string]` — Bump a semver version by the specified part.
- `dybatpho::semver_release_type <string> <string>` — Detect the release type between two semver versions.
- `dybatpho::semver_satisfies <string> <string>` — Return success when a version satisfies a range.
- `dybatpho::semver_sort <string...>` — Print versions in order, lowest first.
- `dybatpho::semver_max <string...>` — Print the highest of a list of versions.
- `dybatpho::semver_coerce <string>` — Normalize a version, as a real command reports it, into a semver string the rest of this module accepts.

## service

Utilities for enabling, controlling and installing services. Loaded: `--modules service`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/service.md](docs/service.md)

- `dybatpho::service_manager` — Print the service manager this machine runs.
- `dybatpho::service_manager_available <string>` — Tell whether the service manager can act in a scope here: it is installed, and running for that scope.
- `dybatpho::service_command <string> <string> <string>` — Print the commands an action would run, one shell-quoted command per line, with the elevation prefix where the action is elevated.
- `dybatpho::service_enable <string> <string>` — Enable a service so it starts at boot or login, and start it now.
- `dybatpho::service_disable <string> <string>` — Disable a service so it no longer starts, and stop it now.
- `dybatpho::service_start <string> <string>` — Start a service now, without enabling it.
- `dybatpho::service_stop <string> <string>` — Stop a service now, without disabling it.
- `dybatpho::service_restart <string> <string>` — Restart a service.
- `dybatpho::service_is_active <string> <string>` — Tell whether a service is running now.
- `dybatpho::service_is_enabled <string> <string>` — Tell whether a service is enabled, so it starts at boot or login.
- `dybatpho::service_reload_manager <string>` — Reload the manager's view of its unit files: `daemon-reload` on systemd, nothing elsewhere.
- `dybatpho::service_install <path> <string...>` — Put a unit file or launchd plist where the manager reads it, have the manager pick it up, and enable the service.
- `dybatpho::service_uninstall <string> <string>` — Disable a service, remove the unit file `dybatpho::service_install` put in place, and reload the manager.

## sign

Utilities for signing files and checking signatures. Loaded: `--modules sign`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/sign.md](docs/sign.md)

- `dybatpho::sign_backends [string]` — Print the backends that can sign, or verify, on this machine.
- `dybatpho::sign_file <string> <string> <path> [path]` — Sign a file with a key and print the signature's path.
- `dybatpho::sign_public_key <string> <string>` — Print the value `dybatpho::verify_file` trusts for a key, to pin it in configuration.
- `dybatpho::verify_file <path> <path> <string...>` — Check that a file was signed by one of the trusted keys.

## string

Utilities for working with string. Loaded: always. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/string.md](docs/string.md)

- `dybatpho::trim <string>` — Trim leading and trailing whitespace from a string.
- `dybatpho::split <string> <string>` — Split a string on an exact delimiter.
- `dybatpho::string_starts_with <string> <string>` — Return success when a string starts with the given prefix.
- `dybatpho::string_ends_with <string> <string>` — Return success when a string ends with the given suffix.
- `dybatpho::string_contains <string> <string>` — Return success when a string contains the given substring.
- `dybatpho::string_match <string> <string> <string>` — Match a string against a Bash extended regular expression and hand back what it captured.
- `dybatpho::string_replace <string> <string> <string>` — Replace all exact substring matches in a string.
- `dybatpho::string_trim_prefix <string> <string>` — Remove an exact prefix from a string when it matches.
- `dybatpho::string_trim_suffix <string> <string>` — Remove an exact suffix from a string when it matches.
- `dybatpho::string_slugify <string>` — Convert a string into a lowercase ASCII slug.
- `dybatpho::string_is_blank <string>` — Return success when a string is empty or contains only whitespace.
- `dybatpho::string_trim_chars <string> <string>` — Trim a set of exact characters from both ends of a string.
- `dybatpho::string_truncate <string> <number> [string]` — Truncate a string to a maximum width and append a suffix when needed.
- `dybatpho::string_lines <string>` — Count the number of logical lines in a string.
- `dybatpho::string_wrap <string> <number> [string]` — Wrap a string to a maximum width, normalizing whitespace between words.
- `dybatpho::string_repeat <string> <number>` — Repeat a string a fixed number of times.
- `dybatpho::string_pad <string> <number> [string]` — Pad a string on the right to a minimum width.
- `dybatpho::url_encode <string>` — URL-encode a string.
- `dybatpho::url_decode <string>` — URL-decode a string.
- `dybatpho::lower <string>` — Convert a string to lowercase.
- `dybatpho::upper <string>` — Convert a string to uppercase.
- `dybatpho::string_to_snake <string>` — Convert a string to `snake_case`.
- `dybatpho::string_to_kebab <string>` — Convert a string to `kebab-case`.
- `dybatpho::string_to_camel <string>` — Convert a string to `camelCase`.
- `dybatpho::string_to_pascal <string>` — Convert a string to `PascalCase`.
- `dybatpho::string_quote <string>` — Quote a string so the shell reads it back as one literal value.
- `dybatpho::string_distance <string> <string>` — Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings.
- `dybatpho::string_closest <string> <string> <number> <string...>` — Find the candidates closest to a string by edit distance.

## table

Utilities for rendering aligned plain-text tables. Loaded: `--modules table`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/table.md](docs/table.md)

- `dybatpho::table_print <string> [string]` — Render aligned columns without borders from delimited rows.
- `dybatpho::table_align <string> [string] [string] [number]` — Render aligned columns with optional per-column alignment rules.
- `dybatpho::table_box <string> [string]` — Render a Unicode boxed table from delimited rows.
- `dybatpho::table_markdown <string> [string]` — Render a Markdown table from delimited rows.
- `dybatpho::table_csv <string> [string] [string]` — Render lightweight comma-delimited table data using one of the supported styles.
- `dybatpho::table_from_csv <string> [string] [string]` — Render real CSV as a table, quoting and all.
- `dybatpho::table_from_json <string> [string] [string]` — Render a JSON array of objects as a table.

## testing

Extended assertions, snapshots, mocks, and self-cleaning fixtures for shell tests. Loaded: `--modules testing`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)

- `dybatpho::assert_file <string> [string]` — Assert that a path exists and is a regular file.
- `dybatpho::assert_dir <string> [string]` — Assert that a path exists and is a directory.
- `dybatpho::assert_symlink <string> [string]` — Assert that a path is a symbolic link, optionally pointing at an expected target.
- `dybatpho::assert_path_absent <string>` — Assert that nothing exists at a path.
- `dybatpho::assert_file_contains <string> <string>` — Assert that a file contains an exact substring.
- `dybatpho::assert_file_empty <string>` — Assert that a file exists and holds no content.
- `dybatpho::assert_file_mode <string> <string>` — Assert that a file or directory carries exact octal permissions.
- `dybatpho::assert_json_valid <string>` — Assert that a document is parsable JSON.
- `dybatpho::assert_json_query <string> <string> <string>` — Assert that a JSON query prints an expected value.
- `dybatpho::assert_json_has <string> <string>` — Assert that a JSON filter matches something in the document.
- `dybatpho::assert_yaml_valid <string>` — Assert that a document is parsable YAML.
- `dybatpho::assert_yaml_query <string> <string> <string>` — Assert that a `jq` filter over a YAML document prints an expected value.
- `dybatpho::assert_yaml_has <string> <string>` — Assert that a `jq` filter matches something in a YAML document.
- `dybatpho::snapshot_scrub <string> <string>` — Register a substitution applied to text before it is snapshotted.
- `dybatpho::snapshot_scrub_reset` — Forget every registered snapshot substitution.
- `dybatpho::assert_snapshot <string> <string>` — Compare text against a stored snapshot, creating it when missing.
- `dybatpho::assert_cli_snapshot <string> <string> <string...>` — Snapshot the stdout, stderr, and exit code of a command.
- `dybatpho::assert_exit_code <number> <string> <string...>` — Assert that a command exits with an expected status.
- `dybatpho::assert_duration_under <number> <string> <string...>` — Assert that a command finishes in under a budget of milliseconds.
- `dybatpho::benchmark <string> <number> <string> <string...>` — Time a command over several runs and report its fastest, median, and slowest.
- `dybatpho::mock_env <string...>` — Set environment variables for the duration of a test, remembering their previous state.
- `dybatpho::unmock_env` — Restore every environment variable changed through `dybatpho::mock_env`.
- `dybatpho::test_home [string]` — Point `HOME` and the XDG base directories at a directory of the test's own.
- `dybatpho::test_unset_git_env` — Unset the variables through which git reaches a repository other than the one a command runs in.
- `dybatpho::mock_command_script <string> <string>` — Replace a command with a script that records every invocation.
- `dybatpho::mock_command <string> [number] [string]` — Replace a command with a mock that prints fixed output and exits with a fixed code.
- `dybatpho::mock_calls <string>` — Print one line per recorded invocation of a mocked command.
- `dybatpho::mock_call_count <string>` — Print how many times a mocked command was called.
- `dybatpho::assert_mock_called <string> [string...]` — Assert that a mocked command was called, optionally with specific arguments.
- `dybatpho::unmock_command <string>` — Remove one mocked command so the real command is used again.
- `dybatpho::mock_http <string> <number> [string] [string...]` — Register a canned HTTP response for URLs matching a pattern.
- `dybatpho::mock_http_calls` — Print every URL requested through the HTTP mock, oldest first.
- `dybatpho::mock_http_payloads` — Print the request material of every mocked HTTP call that did not travel in the argument vector, newest last, one request per line.
- `dybatpho::assert_http_called <string>` — Assert that a URL matching a pattern was requested through the HTTP mock.
- `dybatpho::mock_time <number>` — Freeze the clock that `date` reports, for the code under test.
- `dybatpho::mock_time_advance <number>` — Move the frozen clock forward, or back, by a number of seconds.
- `dybatpho::unmock_time` — Unfreeze the clock, so `date` reports the real time again.
- `dybatpho::mock_tty <string> <string...>` — Make the library see a terminal, or none, on the standard streams.
- `dybatpho::unmock_tty` — Give `dybatpho::is_tty` back its real answers.
- `dybatpho::fixture_dir <string>` — Create a temporary fixture directory that is removed when the shell exits.
- `dybatpho::fixture_file <string> <string> [string]` — Create a temporary fixture file holding the given content.
- `dybatpho::unmock_all` — Remove every mock created in this shell and restore the environment, the clock, and the terminal detection.

## text

Utilities for working with multi-line text blocks. Loaded: `--modules text`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/text.md](docs/text.md)

- `dybatpho::text_indent <string> [string]` — Prefix every line in a text block with the given indent string.
- `dybatpho::text_dedent <string>` — Remove the shared leading indentation from a text block.
- `dybatpho::text_strip_ansi <string>` — Strip ANSI escape sequences from a text block.
- `dybatpho::text_bullet_list <string> [string]` — Prefix each non-empty line in a text block as a bullet item.
- `dybatpho::text_columns <string> [string] [number]` — Align a delimited text block into plain columns.
- `dybatpho::text_box <string> [string] [string]` — Draw a border around a text block, with an optional title set into the top edge.
- `dybatpho::text_center <string> [number]` — Center each line of a text block within a width.
- `dybatpho::text_number_lines <string> [number] [string]` — Prefix each line of a text block with its line number.
- `dybatpho::text_truncate_lines <string> <number> [string]` — Keep the first lines of a text block and say how many were left out.

## tui

Interactive terminal widgets: spinners, progress bars, menus, and confirmations. Loaded: `--modules tui`. Stability: experimental. Reference: [docs/tui.md](docs/tui.md)

- `dybatpho::tui_supported` — Return success when the widgets may draw in place and read raw keys, which is what separates the interactive rendering from the fallback.
- `dybatpho::tui_bar <number> <number> [number]` — Render a progress bar as text.
- `dybatpho::tui_spinner_start <string>` — Start a spinner that runs until `dybatpho::tui_spinner_stop` stops it.
- `dybatpho::tui_spinner_message <string>` — Replace the message of the running spinner without restarting it.
- `dybatpho::tui_spinner_stop [number] [string]` — Stop the running spinner, erase its line, and report the outcome.
- `dybatpho::tui_progress_start <string> <number>` — Start a progress bar over a known amount of work.
- `dybatpho::tui_progress_update <number> [string]` — Move the progress bar to an absolute position.
- `dybatpho::tui_progress_step [number] [string]` — Advance the progress bar by a number of units.
- `dybatpho::tui_progress_stop [string]` — Finish the progress bar, leaving the line complete rather than part-drawn.
- `dybatpho::tui_menu <string> <string> <string...>` — Ask the user to pick one entry from a list.
- `dybatpho::tui_multi_menu <string> <string> <string...>` — Ask the user to pick any number of entries from a list.
- `dybatpho::tui_confirm <string> [string]` — Ask a yes/no question with the answer shown as a choice rather than as a `[y/N]` hint.

## validate

One validator for the whole library: named value types and declarative rules. Loaded: `--modules validate`. Stability: stable. Reference: [docs/validate.md](docs/validate.md)

- `dybatpho::validate_matches <string> <string>` — Match a value against an extended regular expression, without letting a malformed expression reach the caller as a shell diagnostic.
- `dybatpho::validate_is <string> <string>` — Return success when a value is of the named type.
- `dybatpho::validate_describe <string>` — Print the noun a message uses for a type, such as `an email address` for `email`.
- `dybatpho::validate_types` — Print every registered type name, one per line, in alphabetical order.
- `dybatpho::validate_register <string> <string> <string> [string]` — Register a type, or replace one that is already registered.
- `dybatpho::validate_value <string> <string...>` — Validate one value against a list of declarative rules, and record every violation rather than stopping at the first.
- `dybatpho::validate_errors` — Print the reasons recorded by the last `dybatpho::validate_value` call, one per line.
- `dybatpho::validate_or_die <string> <string> <string...>` — Validate a value and stop the script when it is rejected, naming what was being validated and every reason it failed.
- `dybatpho::validate_reset` — Forget every type added with `dybatpho::validate_register` and restore the built-ins to their original predicates.
